sample_unit: test sentences (medical abstract sentences, five-class classification)

links.outcome: Accuracy sensitivity to prompt template choice across precisions
links.effect: Prompt choice changed mean accuracy across precisions by 2.9 to 17.8 percentage points between the two primary templates.
links.quote: Between them, prompt choice changes mean accuracy across precisions by 2.9 to 17.8 percentage points.

links.outcome: Accuracy change after quantization (INT8, INT4) versus FP16
links.effect: INT8 changed accuracy by at most 1.1 percentage points for adapted checkpoints; INT4 showed mixed but non-catastrophic effects.
links.quote: Eight-bit quantization changes accuracy by at most 1.1 percentage points for the adapted checkpoints; four-bit quantization shows mixed but non-catastrophic effects.

unlisted_practices: Treating scoring normalization (summed vs mean-token log-likelihood) as an experimental variable when comparing calibration of LLM classifiers

screen.reason: The study tests implementation choices and safeguards (quantization, prompt design, scoring normalization, and post-hoc temperature scaling calibration) on the reliability and calibration of biomedical LLM classification.

primary.practice: post-hoc calibration and scoring rule normalization
